clue.text: In empty surroundings, I will be indecisive

indicators.note: together with 'surroundings', this tells us one piece is placed inside the other
the word for 'empty' forms the surroundings that the 'I will' piece goes into

parts.note: to empty a room is to vacate it
'I will' contracts to I'LL, written as ILL

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a bare, empty place who just cannot make up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is split across the clue, 'In' at the start and 'surroundings' after 'empty'. The apostrophe of the contraction drops out, as crosswords always ignore punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver between options, which is what being indecisive means.

clue.text: Counsellor loses bill for piece of armour

indicators.note: the counsellor word loses the bill word, which is taken out

parts.note: an adviser, also spelt advisor, is a counsellor
an ad is a bill or advertisement, as a poster

explanation.surface: An adviser drops a bill in return for a bit of armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes AD from the front of ADVISOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is the movable front part of a helmet, a piece of armour.

clue.text: Various sorts of angel around, willing to make a commitment

indicators.note: the angel word goes around the anagram, enclosing it

parts.note: cherubic means of or like a cherub, an angel

indicators.note: various sorts are many different arrangements, signalling an anagram

parts.note: someone willing is on, as in 'I'm on for that'

explanation.surface: Different kinds of angels nearby, all keen to sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of angel' is an adjective phrase, so it gives the adjective form of the angel word. 'Various' scrambles 'sorts', 'around' wraps the angel word round that scramble, and 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar crossing the Rubicon river committed him to civil war, so the phrase means taking an irrevocable step.

clue.text: Tendency to absorb only one of the basics to get scholarship

indicators.note: the tendency word takes in, or absorbs, the single letter

parts.note: a leaning is a tendency or inclination
the basics are the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, so one of them is R

explanation.surface: An inclination to soak up just one fundamental skill to win a scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the three Rs' is a traditional name for the basics of education. 'to absorb' puts R inside LEANING.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning means knowledge gained by study, the same as scholarship in its sense of erudition.

clue.text: Hero is sick, beset by pains

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the pains word wraps round the sick word

parts.note: pains are aches
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A hero taken ill, surrounded by aches and pains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; 'beset by' means the pains word surrounds the sick word.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the great Greek hero of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Drink, say, taken before invitation to dinner crops up

indicators.note: the 'say' piece is taken before, coming ahead of, the next piece

parts.note: EG, for example, is signalled by 'say'

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that crops up rises, so the word reads upward, backwards

parts.note: a gong is struck to call people to dinner

explanation.surface: A drink is mentioned just before the dinner call is heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crops up' turns GONG upward in this down clue, giving GNOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a drink of eggs, milk, sugar and often spirits, popular at Christmas.

clue.text: Car park is a long walk

parts.note: a tram is a car that runs on rails, and in the US a streetcar
P is the standard abbreviation for park, as on parking signs

explanation.surface: A claim that walking from the car park is a long trek.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long, tiring walk, as in 'a tramp across the moors'.

clue.text: Craving new T-shirt

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A longing for a new T-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst can mean a strong desire or craving, as in a thirst for knowledge.

clue.text: Actually, a modicum of knowledge brought about a cancelled operation

indicators.note: brought about means placed around, so the first two pieces enclose the second 'a'

parts.note: a smatter, or smattering, is a slight knowledge
an event that is cancelled is off
an act is an operation or deed

explanation.surface: A little knowledge led to a medical procedure being called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a' looks like part of 'a cancelled operation' but goes inside the first two pieces, which 'brought about' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: 'As a matter of fact' is an idiom meaning actually or in reality.

clue.text: Rat-catcher is good bloke, good person

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good in crossword usage
Ed is a man's name, standing for any bloke
pi again, short for pious
per means for each person, as in 'per capita'

explanation.surface: A rat-catcher described as a decent chap and a good sort.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword favourite for good. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pied Piper of Hamelin lured the town's rats away with his pipe music, so he is the famous rat-catcher.

clue.text: Inside, mac's hot — change it

indicators.note: being told to change it means the letters before it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone indoors, overheating in a mac, is told to take it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram ignores the apostrophe in 'mac's', leaving the seven letters MACSHOT. 'it' just points back at those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside can be a noun meaning the belly or innards, and the stomach is the main one.

clue.text: Face of stern expert

parts.note: a stern look is a grim one
an ace is an expert at something

explanation.surface: A description of the face of a strict specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a noun but here it is a verb: to grimace is to make a twisted face.
explanation.definitionFit: To grimace is to pull a face, usually in pain or disgust.

clue.text: Proved to be up

definitions.meaning: dough that has proved has ... before baking
someone who is up has got out of bed, as the sun is up after dawn

explanation.definitionFit: Proved dough has swelled upward, and a person who is up has got out of bed.

clue.text: Hurry up and free shark caught in noose

indicators.note: something caught in the noose sits inside the word for noose

parts.note: a noose is a loop of rope

indicators.note: to free the word shark is to let its letters loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Urging a quick rescue of a shark tangled in a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' scrambles 'shark' and 'caught in' puts the scrambled letters inside the noose word. 'Hurry up' looks like part of the instructions but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Look sharp!' is an idiom telling someone to hurry up and be quick about it.

clue.text: Door may be 23

definitions.meaning: a door taken off its hinges is literally hinge-less
the answer to 23 down means crazy, deranged

explanation.walkthrough: 23 refers to NUTTY, the answer to 23 down, meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A door off its hinges is literally so, and the word also means mentally unbalanced, the crazy sense of 23.

clue.text: Stars and stripes may be 23

definitions.meaning: the American flag may be flying high on its flagpole
the answer to 23 down means crazy, deranged

explanation.walkthrough: 23 refers to NUTTY, the answer to 23 down, meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag flies at the top of its pole, and the phrase is British slang for mad, the crazy sense of 23.

clue.text: Prevent trophies being rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: sporting trophies are often called pots, as cups are

explanation.surface: Stopping a team's cups from being refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rejected' turns POTS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something happening is to prevent it.

clue.text: Mare, most unusually, produces rather small creature

indicators.note: set out unusually, the letters take an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A horse that, against all odds, gives birth to a tiny animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small monkey of South America, a fairly small creature.

clue.text: Materialise with heavenly body —- and wish it hadn't, happened

parts.note: a comet is a heavenly body
to rue something is to regret it, to wish it hadn't happened

explanation.surface: Something appears along with a comet, and you then regret it.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma in the second piece is just OCR noise from the page: read 'wish it hadn't happened'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come true is for a hope or prediction to become real, to materialise.

clue.text: Go off and become fit

definitions.meaning: milk that goes off has gone sour
to ... nasty is to become nasty
a ... is a sudden attack of illness, like a funny ...

explanation.definitionFit: Milk turns when it sours, people turn grey as they age, and a funny turn is a brief fit.

clue.text: Party given by queen for Hercules, perhaps?

parts.note: Labour is one of the main UK political parties
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Asking whether a party offered by the queen was meant for the hero Hercules.
explanation.walkthrough: Hercules performed twelve labours, so the setter calls him a labourer, with a question mark to show this is a playful example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules famously carried out twelve Labours, making him a heroic worker in a punning sense.

clue.text: A stratagem discussed briefly

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken out, so we hear how the words sound

parts.note: a wile is a stratagem or trick

explanation.surface: A tactic talked over in short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discussed' says that A WILE is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Awhile means for a short time, which is how briefly is used here.

clue.text: It's an even chance drunk turns up with drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunk
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A drunkard staggering in with a drink is a fifty-fifty matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses SOT to TOS; 'It's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is a situation as uncertain as tossing a coin, an even chance.

clue.text: Lower boom awkwardly to provide sufficient space

indicators.note: done awkwardly, the two words are clumsily jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors told to lower a sail's boom carefully so there is room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move freely without being cramped.

clue.text: Just mischievous? Myself, I never accept that

indicators.note: the words accept, or take in, the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they are merely naughty firmly denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'mysELF, I Never'; 'that' points back to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like an elf, small and a little impish, so 'just mischievous' with a question mark fits.

clue.text: Uranium — tons and tons found in state like Brazil

indicators.note: pieces found in another piece sit inside it

parts.note: NY is New York state
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
T is the abbreviation for ton
T again, for ton

explanation.surface: Uranium in great quantities discovered in a Brazilian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts UTT inside NY. Brazil is a kind of nut, the misleading definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil nut is nutty, so the country's name stands for the nut here.

clue.text: Flowers concealed amongst monsters

indicators.note: one piece placed amongst another goes inside it

parts.note: orcs are monsters of fantasy fiction, as in Tolkien
concealed means hid

explanation.surface: Blooms tucked away among fearsome beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' looks like a hidden-word signal but is a synonym, the past tense of hide; 'amongst' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchids are a large family of showy flowering plants.

clue.text: Attendant working in taverns

indicators.note: working, the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bar staff employed in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is someone who attends to another, an attendant.

clue.text: Lake acquiring new name

indicators.note: the lake word acquires the extra letter by taking it inside

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A lake being given a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquiring' puts N inside ERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a man's first name, short for Ernest.

clue.text: One is put in openly, without complaint

indicators.note: the word for one is put inside the word for openly

parts.note: patently means openly, obviously
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone placed somewhere in full view, putting up with it quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put in' puts I inside PATENTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something patiently means bearing it calmly without complaint.
